mode.note: enumeration by convention; never a boolean

directives.detail: Pads on the right so the next value occupies n columns.
gotchas: Padding counts terminal display columns, not bytes and not characters. SGR escape sequences contribute zero columns -- verified: a pad of 20 over a coloured 8-character subject produced exactly 12 spaces.
Without a truncation option, padding never shortens: an over-long value is emitted in full and the column budget is simply exceeded.

Truncation is character-aligned and can OVERSHOOT the requested width on wide glyphs. Verified across N=1..40: a 14-column request on a CJK subject yields 15 columns, and 16 yields 17. git never splits a UTF-8 sequence. No simple rule is stated here because none was found; the behaviour is pinned by golden vectors instead (spec F-6).
Minimum output is the ellipsis itself -- N of 1 or 2 both render '..'.
